nodes.func: **new async override with one private transient candidate.** Initialize no other app/session attribute. `_right_gesture` is either `None` or one record containing `text`, `screen_offset`, `screen`, `widget` and `valid`. On every not-forwarded `events.MouseDown`, first clear any old candidate; a non-button-3 press leaves it cleared. On button 3 only, before any toolkit forwarding, capture `screen = self.screen`, the widget returned by `screen.get_widget_at(event.screen_x, event.screen_y)`, `screen_offset = event.screen_offset`, and `text = N2(event.screen_x, event.screen_y)`, storing one fresh candidate with `valid=True`; N2 retains its early text-box exclusion and returns either non-empty text or `None`. Do not call N1 on `MouseDown`. On every `events.MouseMove` with a candidate, if `event.screen_offset != candidate.screen_offset`, set only `valid=False`; never restore it on a later move, even to the original offset. On every not-forwarded `events.MouseUp`, first copy the candidate to a local and set `_right_gesture = None`, consuming it before any possible N1 call. Call N1 once only when `event.button == 3`, a candidate exists, `candidate.valid` is true, its text is non-empty, and the release has the same `screen_offset`, the identical current screen and the identical widget from `get_widget_at` at the release coordinates. Different offset/screen/widget, a `None` text, any invalidated drag, a replayed release and every forwarded release copy nothing. N3 does not stop/prevent events, synthesize clicks, await C1 or handle `Click`; every event path, including keys, pastes, forwarded events, invalid gestures and the path that calls N1, finishes with exactly one `await super().on_event(event)`. Back-to-back behavior is preserved because the press snapshots before its superclass forward and the matching release calls N1 before its own superclass forward clears the selection.
